threats.title: Time-transfer message offset or asymmetry on satellite clocks
threats.mechanism: Manipulating or delaying inter-satellite time transfer shifts a satellite clock without breaking any message authentication, creating a range bias on every observable it stamps.

threats.title: GNSS-based manipulation of onboard clock discipline
threats.mechanism: Corrupting the GNSS timing input that disciplines the onboard oscillator introduces a small covert clock step that stays below onboard consistency checks.

threats.title: Weakening of synchronisation policy and conformance thresholds
threats.mechanism: An insider or intruder loosens the time scale, PTP policy or GNSS-PTP conformance limits so that a clock offset is accepted as conformant.

threats.title: Malicious telecommand or software-update injection
threats.mechanism: Forged, replayed or compromised command and update packages alter payload or bus behaviour, including clock, extraction or filter settings, giving control of the command path.

threats.title: Tampering with integrity thresholds and filter parameters
threats.mechanism: Changing stored thresholds or filter settings widens the undetected region of the integrity monitor, so a bias raises no flag and the integrity annotation stays nominal.

threats.title: Exploiting weak-geometry stealth window
threats.mechanism: An adversary times or selects a bias for passes with poor geometry, where the stated analysis admits an undetectable region, to cause displacement with a nominal annotation.

threats.title: Coordinated multi-satellite or common-mode bias beyond single-fault model
threats.mechanism: Several consistent biases, or a common-mode clock fault, can pass residual tests designed around a single-satellite fault, contradicting the single-bias detection assumption.

threats.title: Coordinated displacement with consistent falsified self-report
threats.mechanism: A deceived or colluding aircraft broadcasts content that agrees with the biased independent position, so the cross-check finds no discrepancy and the annotation stays nominal.

threats.title: Payload extraction firmware implant
threats.mechanism: A supply-chain or insider modification of the extraction firmware biases timestamps or measurements, or hides faults, from inside the payload processor.

threats.title: Compromise or exfiltration of keys and credentials
threats.mechanism: Theft or misuse of telecommand, ISL or ground-link keys enables later forgery and removes authentication as a defence. Disclosure is a precondition of other threats.

threats.title: In-transit modification of unauthenticated observable reports
threats.mechanism: Because reports carry no message authentication, a link or backhaul adversary can alter measurements or metadata between the payload and the processing station.

threats.title: Poisoning of orbit-determination products
threats.mechanism: Corrupted ephemeris products feed a position or clock-state error into the localisation solver. The error is not visible to onboard checks.

threats.title: Tampering with the ephemeris and clock-state database
threats.mechanism: Direct modification of stored satellite state shifts the solved position consistently across solutions and may stay inside residual tolerances.

threats.title: Association confusion between receptions of different transmissions
threats.mechanism: Decoys, near-simultaneous emissions or replays cause receptions to be grouped wrongly across satellites, producing wrong or ghost positions that appear internally consistent.

threats.title: Delayed replay of recorded emissions
threats.mechanism: Re-radiated recorded signals produce receptions with the wrong time of arrival and valid content, displacing a genuine target or duplicating it.

threats.title: Synchronised multi-emitter generation of ghost targets
threats.mechanism: Several time-synchronised emitters create signals whose arrival pattern is consistent with a fabricated aircraft at a chosen location, defeating single-emitter plausibility checks.

threats.title: Driving tracker divergence with crafted measurement sequences
threats.mechanism: Sequences of plausible measurements exploit the EKF/IMM motion-model switching and gating to pull the track away from the true position without triggering residual alarms.

threats.title: Manipulation of the ASTERIX integrity indicator
threats.mechanism: Altering or forcing the encoded integrity annotation, or stripping flags, makes degraded or suspect reports appear nominal to ATM.

threats.title: Compromise of the processing station hosting platform
threats.mechanism: Compromise of servers or virtualisation gives control over all hosted L3 modules, bypassing their internal checks and trust boundaries.

threats.title: Hijack of ground-station uplink path
threats.mechanism: Control of ground antennas and modems, or a spoofed uplink, allows commands to reach satellites outside the normal operations chain.

threats.title: On-orbit bus and flight software compromise
threats.mechanism: Exploiting flight software or the telecommand receiver gives control of the bus and the payload it hosts and commands.

threats.title: Interception or modification of the ATM data feed
threats.mechanism: Altering or injecting reports on the delivery path to ATM bypasses upstream integrity logic, at the outer trust boundary with the consumer.

threats.title: Insider misuse of authorised access to configuration
threats.mechanism: A privileged person or supplier changes thresholds, ephemeris or firmware baselines and may remove traces, using legitimate credentials.

threats.title: Supplier software supply-chain compromise
threats.mechanism: A trojanised update or component from a supplier reaches the processing platform or tools through the normal update route.

threats.title: Intrusion into operations centre via remote access
threats.mechanism: Compromise of workstations, remote access or the management network gives a foothold over the synchronisation, orbit, key and configuration systems hosted there.

threats.title: GNSS denial forcing clock holdover and PTP reliance
threats.mechanism: Jamming the GNSS input removes one of two clock references, shifting trust to time transfer and exposing the clocks to drift in holdover.

threats.title: Falsified clock-quality metadata in reports
threats.mechanism: Misreported clock-quality fields hide an offset from processing-side checks that rely on the metadata. This acts as an enabler.

threats.title: Channel saturation exhausting extraction capacity
threats.mechanism: A high rate of valid-looking or overlapping 1090 MHz signals overloads decoding and reporting, reducing coverage below the requirement.

threats.title: Tampering or replay on inter-satellite links
threats.mechanism: A link adversary delays, drops, replays or alters relayed reports on crosslinks, degrading coverage or corrupting the measurement set.

threats.title: Regional jamming of the 1090 MHz band
threats.mechanism: Local interference blocks reception of aircraft emissions in a region, so targets are lost or coverage falls below the requirement.

threats.title: Jamming of downlinks and ground antennas
threats.mechanism: Interference at ground stations or on the downlink delays or blocks report delivery, degrading observability for affected satellites.

threats.title: Angle-of-arrival distortion by directional emitters
threats.mechanism: Emitters positioned or steered relative to the array bias angle-of-arrival estimates, adding inconsistency or a consistent position error through the beamforming stage.

threats.title: Aircraft broadcasting a falsified self-reported position
threats.mechanism: A deceptive aircraft transmits wrong content. The independent position should expose the discrepancy, so impact depends on the integrity indicator.

threats.title: Deceived aircraft through GNSS spoofing causing false discrepancies
threats.mechanism: A genuine aircraft with spoofed GNSS reports a wrong position, raising false discrepancy flags that may discredit a real target or mask a deceptive one.

threats.title: Track database tampering
threats.mechanism: Altering stored tracks or tracker state after solving changes what is reported without touching any measurement.

threats.title: Induced false verdicts in the cross-check
threats.mechanism: Manipulated inputs make the cross-check mark genuine aircraft as inconsistent or accept inconsistent ones, so the integrity indicator becomes unreliable.

threats.title: Natural clock faults masking or mimicking a malicious offset
threats.mechanism: Radiation, thermal or ageing effects produce genuine drifts that raise the detection thresholds or create plausible cover for a malicious offset.

threats.title: Denial of service on the ATM feed
threats.mechanism: Flooding or disrupting the delivery path removes or delays surveillance reports at the controller position.

threats.title: Induced nuisance alerts eroding controller trust
threats.mechanism: Ghost targets or false integrity flags create spurious conflict alerts and workload, degrading trust in the picture or prompting the controller to switch it off.

threats.title: Social engineering of operator staff
threats.mechanism: Deceiving personnel yields credentials or approvals for configuration or access changes, giving a low-cost entry to L3 and L4.

threats.title: Audit-log tampering and attribution loss
threats.mechanism: Removing or altering logs and key-use records prevents attribution of configuration or key misuse and delays detection of other threats. This acts as an enabler.

threats.title: Compromise of ground-station modem firmware
threats.mechanism: Modified modem or antenna-controller firmware can drop, alter or leak traffic at the satellite-ground boundary.

threats.title: Disclosure of precise ephemerides and ephemeris data
threats.mechanism: Leakage of precise satellite states lets an adversary calculate observable signal geometry for later emitter-side deception. This is a precondition for other threats.

threats.title: Eavesdropping on downlink revealing system health
threats.mechanism: Observing unencrypted report traffic exposes clock-quality metadata and coverage, which helps an adversary choose timing and region of attack.

threats.title: Replay of stale reports over the backhaul
threats.mechanism: Re-injecting earlier valid reports into the ground network can corrupt association or the track, if freshness is not enforced.

architecture_weaknesses: Unauthenticated ADS-B and observables (W4): authentication cannot remove time-offset threats, since the authentication-invariance test shows the temporal class survives sound cryptography.
W2 assumes a single-satellite bias. Coordinated multi-satellite or common-mode biases and combinations with ephemeris error are not covered by the stated detection guarantee.
W3 concedes an undetectable window in weak geometry, but the design offers no mitigation, such as geometry-dependent degradation of the integrity indicator or suppression of output.
W1 rests on a literature step size, possibly from analogue evidence. Ramps, smaller steps or other sizes may escape checks, and the fixed h* depends on one assumed step.
The cross-check relies on the unauthenticated ADS-B self-report and a single integrity indicator, so both its input and its output are single points of failure.
Governance (L4) can set thresholds, ephemeris, keys and configuration through channel C across a single TB3 boundary, concentrating risk in insiders, the key store and the operations network.
Onboard time depends on only two inputs, GNSS and PTP, with no independent third reference or ground truth to detect a common failure or coordinated manipulation of both.
The fixed e_req = 350 m and h* treat the ephemeris error budget and natural clock faults as separate from the adversary, so misattribution and cover for attacks are not modelled.
overall: The timing dependency is the central risk: authentication does not remove it, and the stated detection assumptions W1 to W3 are optimistic. Governance and insider paths can silently weaken checks, and the cross-check shares failure modes with the data it verifies. Priorities are independent time references, multi-fault integrity tests and hardened L4 controls.
